subject: Re: Sudden P95/P99 latency surge — possible prefix cache eviction

Subject: High P99 spikes since 10:00 PT — production impact

Alex —

We started seeing a sharp jump in P95/P99 latency on the hosted endpoints around 10:00 PT this morning. Nothing in our deploy schedule changed on our side. The backend error rate also rose ~2x for short bursts (20–30s). Attaching a short screenshot of the P99 graph.

This is affecting our checkout flow (payments microservice) and we need an ETA on a mitigation. Can you escalate?

Thanks,

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: RE: High P99 spikes since 10:00 PT — production impact

Quick update from infra: we pulled the trace window around the incident. Initial signs point to a sudden increase in full KV lookups (misses) for long prefixes — the serving runtime shows a spike in cold-KV fetch latency starting at 09:58 PT.

What changed?
- Config canary deployed at ~09:50 PT toggled a prefix-cache TTL parameter (canary-config-diff attached). It appears the TTL was set to 0 for the canary, which forces immediate eviction instead of soft-expiry. The canary rolled to ~10% of traffic.
- When the canary scaled under load we saw localized cache thrashing: frequent evictions and re-population, which amplified tail latency.

Suggested mitigation (short):
1) Disable the canary config flip (roll back TTL change) — can be done immediately.
2) Warm the prefix cache for outstanding hot prefixes (we can push a warmup job).
3) Temporarily bump canary to 0% and monitor p95/p99 for 30m.

I've attached a debug snapshot (redwood_debug_snapshot.tar.gz) and the config diff. Diego, can you confirm the rollback and trigger the warmup?

— Dylan (on-call infra)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: High P99 spikes since 10:00 PT — production impact

Rolled back the canary TTL flip at 15:02 PT and initiated a prefix warmup for Acme's top 50 prefixes (based on recent traffic). Early telemetry: p95 dropped back to baseline within ~5 minutes; p99 is trending down but still has a few outliers.

Actions taken:
- Canary config reverted (canary -> 0%).
- Warmup job submitted to the prefix cache worker pool (jobs queued across regions).
- Instrumented additional KV metrics and elevated trace sampling for Acme tenant for next 2 hours.

I'll keep the warmup monitored. If p99 doesn't normalize within 30–45m we'll consider a temporary regional routing change (route Acme traffic to a less-impacted pool).

— Diego
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Kline <maya@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@acmeretail.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High P99 spikes since 10:00 PT — production impact

Maya — thank you for your patience. Engineering identified that a canary config flip reduced prefix cache TTL to 0 (forcing eviction) which created a cache-eviction storm as the canary scaled. We rolled the canary back at 15:02 PT and primed the hot-prefixes.

Status now: p95 is back to baseline; p99 has improved significantly and is expected to stabilize in the next 20–30 minutes. Diego is keeping elevated tracing for your tenant.

Next steps for us (I'll follow-up in a formal post-mortem):
- Full post-mortem and root-cause analysis will be shared by Monday.
- We'll add a gating rule to prevent TTL=0 flips on canaries for prefixes serving live traffic.
- Offer a one-time credit for the impacted time window (I will coordinate with finance/CS).

If you still see anything odd, please ping me directly and I'll escalate again.

— Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
